q: I'm shooting F-Log2 next weekend and want a dark, moody grade later. How should I expose?
a: 1. Expose brighter than looks 'normal': skin and subject about +1 stop above a standard profile is common for F-Log2, with zebras / the histogram keeping highlights from clipping. 2. Bring it down in the grade: Revolution normalises the log with colour management, then you set exposure and the mood on the nodes. 3. Why: log's shadows are noisy, so more light means a cleaner dark grade; if shadows still crawl, noise reduction helps. Bright is fine, clipped isn't: clipped highlights can't come back.

q: should i bake the fuji LUT into the recording so it looks right straight away
a: No: record log (F-Log2) and use the camera LUT only to monitor on set. Baking it in throws the extra range away for good. Revolution reads the clip's colour space and converts it in its working space, so no LUT is needed in the edit; a LUT on a node is for looks.

q: Night scene planned in F-Log2. How do I keep the shadows clean for a low-key grade?
a: Add light rather than relying on the grade: expose the subject brighter (about +1 stop for F-Log2) without clipping the practical lights, then take it down in the grade with Gamma and Lift. Log shadows are noisy, so underexposing and lifting later shows noise; if they still crawl after the grade, use noise reduction.

q: I have 40 minutes of vlog footage and want a 6-minute video fast. Where do I start?
a: 1. Watch everything once and mark only the good moments: markers in the Source monitor (M, `markers.add`) or Make Subclip (`clip.makeSubclip`) into a selects bin; be strict. 2. Lay the selects on the timeline in order. 3. Tighten from the keyboard: park the playhead where a moment should start or end and Ripple Trim Previous / Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.ripplePrevious`, `trim.rippleNext`), which cuts and closes the gap. 4. Watch it through and tighten again in a later pass.

q: fastest way to chop the boring bits out of a long talking clip with the keyboard
a: Play with J / K / L, and at the start of a boring bit add an edit (`sequence.addEdit`); at its end use Ripple Trim Previous Edit to Playhead (`trim.ripplePrevious`): the bit is gone and the gap closed in one key. The plain Trim versions leave a gap, safer when other tracks must not move.

q: Premiere has 'Ripple Trim Previous Edit to Playhead'. Same thing for a quick vlog rough cut here?
a: Yes: Ripple Trim Previous / Next Edit to Playhead (`trim.ripplePrevious`, `trim.rippleNext`) cut from the playhead to the nearest edit and close the gap; Trim Previous / Next (`trim.previous`, `trim.next`) do it leaving a gap. Extend Selected Edit to Playhead (`trim.extendToPlayhead`) moves an edit point to the playhead.
